battery_light.description: Tested claim: ambient light level is inferable from battery voltage/current/temperature telemetry (via display auto-brightness power draw). Falsified: no measurable information gain over the prior once display brightness is held fixed or the ambient light sensor baseline is available.
limitations: Apparent signal in pilot data was entirely mediated by auto-brightness display power draw, not by any direct physical coupling; with brightness fixed, mutual information estimate fell below the screening threshold.
battery_light.name: Ambient Light from Battery Telemetry
references: Screening run 2026-07-12, MI estimate 0.02 bits vs threshold 0.1 bits
battery_light.task: ambient light level: dark / dim / bright

cpu_contention_sensor_v1.description: Infers the number of concurrent compute tenants contending for the CPU from the shape of a fixed workload's timing distribution — no /proc, no cgroup, no OS load API. The designed use of a busy loop is computation; the latent use is a contention sensor. Certified on this host under a cross-time-block split.
failure_modes: A fully idle host with a constant background daemon could shift the noise floor.
limitations: Measured on one CPU (Intel Xeon @ 2.80GHz, 4 cores, Linux 6.18) in a container.
Cross-CPU / cross-host generalization not yet certified (single-device scope).
Absolute contention counts assume a comparable core count.

model.features: mean/std/median/p90/p99, mean-over-median & p90-over-median ratios, stall fraction
model.kind: random forest over timing-distribution shape features

cpu_contention_sensor_v1.name: CPU Contention Sensor (timing jitter)

privacy_audit.bystander_inference: Reveals the presence and count of co-resident compute tenants on the same host without any OS load API — a noisy-neighbor / co-tenancy side channel.
privacy_audit.escalation_gradient: Finer time resolution and per-core pinning could fingerprint specific neighbor workloads or build a covert channel; not demonstrated here.
privacy_audit.mitigations: Coarsen the clock exposed to untrusted code; add scheduler noise; pin tenants to disjoint cores.

cpu_contention_sensor_v1.task: cpu contention level: 0 / 1 / 2 / 3 extra busy cores

cpu_contention_unpinned_v1.description: Naive contention sensor with the measurer NOT pinned to the load's core. Background burners land on other cores, so the fixed workload is barely perturbed and the capability fails to generalize across time blocks — the falsifier rejects it. Kept as a negative result: the physical insight (same-core contention) is what mattered.
failure_modes: A fully idle host with a constant background daemon could shift the noise floor.
limitations: Measured on one CPU (Intel Xeon @ 2.80GHz, 4 cores, Linux 6.18) in a container.
Cross-CPU / cross-host generalization not yet certified (single-device scope).
Absolute contention counts assume a comparable core count.
cpu_contention_unpinned_v1.name: CPU Contention Sensor — unpinned (naive)
cpu_contention_unpinned_v1.task: cpu contention level: 0 / 1 / 2 / 3 extra busy cores

cpu_jitter_entropy_v1.description: Harvests physical entropy from nanosecond jitter in the time to run a fixed CPU workload. Designed use of the clock is timekeeping; the latent capability is a true-random source. LSB is von-Neumann-whitened; min-entropy and a randomness battery are measured on the whitened stream.
failure_modes: A CPU with a very coarse timer (low-resolution perf_counter) would starve the LSB of entropy.

generalization.note: single-host measurement; cross-CPU generalization is future work

limitations: Measured on one CPU (Intel Xeon @ 2.80GHz, Linux 6.18) in a container; cross-CPU min-entropy not yet certified.
Raw throughput is low; suitable for seeding a CSPRNG, not bulk generation.

model.features: low bit of perf_counter_ns workload timing

cpu_jitter_entropy_v1.name: CPU Timing-Jitter Entropy Source

privacy_audit.bystander_inference: None — the source consumes only its own timing; it reveals nothing about other parties.
privacy_audit.escalation_gradient: The same fixed-workload timing channel that yields entropy also leaks contention information (see exp_hw_loadsense); an attacker co-resident on the host could use it as a covert/side timing channel.
privacy_audit.mitigations: Whiten before use (von Neumann here; a cryptographic conditioner such as SHA-256 in deployment). Do not expose raw timings across trust boundaries.

memory_hierarchy_v1.description: Recovers this machine's cache/memory hierarchy from a pointer-chase latency sweep over geometrically growing working sets — no CPUID, no /proc, no vendor spec. The designed use of a memory walk is data access; the latent capability is empirical microarchitecture discovery: a flat cache-resident plateau and a cache->DRAM latency cliff whose working-set boundary reproduces across independent runs.
failure_modes: A host whose L3 exceeds the max swept working set would hide the cliff.
Heavy co-tenant memory-bandwidth load can blur the plateau and shift the boundary.

generalization.note: single-host measurement; the boundary and latencies are this CPU's own topology

limitations: Measured on one host (4 logical cores, Linux 6.18) in a container; the absolute latency floor includes a constant Python-interpreter overhead, so sub-cliff levels (L1/L2) sit inside the flat region and are not individually resolved.
Recovers the dominant cache->DRAM boundary + its latency ratio, not the full per-level cache-size table; cross-CPU generalization not certified.
The certified quantity is the reproducible cliff ratio; the boundary itself carries ~one-octave run-to-run noise (observed ~2-16 MiB) on this shared host.

model.features: median ns/access vs working-set size (geometric ladder)
model.kind: pointer-chase latency sweep + largest-jump tier detection

memory_hierarchy_v1.name: Memory-Hierarchy Ladder (recovered from timing)

privacy_audit.bystander_inference: None about other parties — the probe only walks its own memory and times its own accesses; it reveals the host's cache topology, not any neighbor's data.
privacy_audit.escalation_gradient: The same working-set-latency structure is the substrate of cache timing side channels (e.g. Prime+Probe); this experiment only maps the hierarchy on its own host and demonstrates no cross-tenant attack.
privacy_audit.mitigations: Constant-time memory access patterns in secret-dependent code; cache partitioning / way-locking; coarsen the clock exposed to untrusted code.

memory_hierarchy_v1.task: recover the cache/memory hierarchy (level-transition boundary + latencies)

occupancy_room_echo_trap.description: Planted memorization trap: room_echo encodes room identity. Rejected by the falsifier — perfect within known rooms, collapses on a new room.
limitations: Room-bound; do not deploy outside its certified room set.
occupancy_room_echo_trap.name: Occupancy from room_echo (planted trap)

occupancy_sim_v1.description: Estimates occupancy class (0/1/2/3+) from WiFi RSSI, thermal, and IMU. Simulated validation of the CCS pipeline.

model.features: rssi var/mean, thermal mean, imu band energy

occupancy_sim_v1.name: Room Occupancy (simulated)

privacy_audit.bystander_inference: Reveals presence and coarse count of non-consenting occupants; no identity.
privacy_audit.escalation_gradient: Higher IMU rate + per-AP RSSI could localize occupants; not demonstrated.
privacy_audit.mitigations: Cap IMU at 100 Hz; quantize RSSI to 2 dBm.

occupancy_v1.description: Estimates room occupancy class (0 / 1 / 2 / 3+ people) from low-intrusion signals: WiFi RSSI perturbation, battery thermal drift, and micro-vibration via accelerometer. No microphone, no camera.
failure_modes: Aggressive WiFi scan throttling on some OEM power-saver modes starves the RSSI feature.
limitations: Requires the phone to be stationary on a surface in the room.
Accuracy degrades when HVAC state changes mid-window.

model.features: RSSI variance + spectral entropy, thermal slope, accel band energy 0.5-4 Hz
model.kind: gradient-boosted trees over 10 s windowed features

occupancy_v1.name: Room Occupancy Estimation

privacy_audit.bystander_inference: Reveals presence and coarse count of non-consenting room occupants; does not identify individuals at the recommended operating point.
privacy_audit.escalation_gradient: Higher IMU rates plus per-AP RSSI could support coarse localization of occupants within the room; identification not demonstrated.
privacy_audit.mitigations: Cap IMU at 100 Hz and quantize RSSI to 2 dBm; occupancy accuracy retained, localization escalation degrades below baseline.

sustained_contention_v1.description: Aggregates the CPU contention sensor over 3 consecutive windows to report sustained co-tenancy. Built by the capability algebra (temporal-integration, confidence upper bound 0.9943); not yet independently falsified, hence experimental.
limitations: Algebra bound only; awaiting its own falsification run.
sustained_contention_v1.name: Sustained CPU Contention (temporal integration)
sustained_contention_v1.task: sustained cpu contention over a 3-window horizon

timer_resolution_v1.description: Recovers the effective granularity of perf_counter_ns by reading it back-to-back and taking the smallest nonzero delta — the real tick the OS/CPU expose, not the advertised one. The median delta is the read overhead.
failure_modes: A coarse-timer platform (low-resolution clock) would fail the sub-µs bar.
limitations: Measured on one host (Linux 6.18) in a container; the Python read overhead sets a floor on the observable resolution.
timer_resolution_v1.name: Effective Clock Resolution (recovered from timing)

privacy_audit.bystander_inference: None — it times only its own clock reads.
privacy_audit.escalation_gradient: A fine clock is the enabler of most timing side channels; that is why coarse clocks are a standard mitigation.
privacy_audit.mitigations: Coarsen the clock exposed to untrusted code (reduce timestamp resolution).

timer_resolution_v1.task: recover the effective clock resolution + read overhead

workload_type_classifier_v1.description: Classifies a co-located neighbor's workload type — idle / cpu_bound / memory_bound — from two self-timing micro-probes: a register-bound arithmetic probe (a CPU-bound neighbor preempts the measurer, inflating the timing tail) and an ~8 MB pointer-chase memory probe (a memory-bandwidth neighbor lifts the memory-probe median). The designed uses of a busy loop and a memory walk are computation and access; the latent use is neighbor-workload diagnosis. Certified on this host under a cross-time-block split. Defensive observability only — no /proc, no cgroup, no cross-process channel.
failure_modes: A neighbor that is both CPU- and memory-intensive blends the two signatures.
Aggressive clock coarsening removes the tail/median structure the probes rely on.
limitations: Measured on one CPU (4 logical cores, Linux 6.18) in a container where CPU affinity is only advisory; contention is created by oversubscription, not pinning.
Cross-CPU / cross-host generalization not certified (single-device scope).
cpu_bound relies on scheduler preemption tails; a host with abundant spare cores may make a CPU-bound neighbor harder to distinguish from idle.

model.features: per-probe mean/std/median, mean-over-median & p90-over-median ratios, floor ratio
model.kind: random forest over two-probe timing-distribution shape features

workload_type_classifier_v1.name: Co-located Workload-Type Classifier (timing micro-probes)

privacy_audit.bystander_inference: Reveals the *type* of a co-resident workload (idle / cpu-bound / memory-bound) on the same host from self-timing alone — a noisy-neighbor diagnosis / observability side channel. It does not read the neighbor's data or identify it.
privacy_audit.escalation_gradient: Finer time resolution or per-probe fingerprinting could in principle profile a specific neighbor workload or build a covert channel; not demonstrated here and out of scope for this defensive observability use.
privacy_audit.mitigations: Coarsen the clock exposed to untrusted code; partition shared LLC / memory bandwidth (e.g. cache/bandwidth allocation); schedule tenants on disjoint cores.

workload_type_classifier_v1.task: co-located workload type: idle / cpu_bound / memory_bound
